{{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | map_size = | title = [[Governor of New Hampshire|Governor]] | before_election = [[Chris Sununu]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Kelly Ayotte]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in New Hampshire}} The '''2024 New Hampshire gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2024 to elect the [[governor of New Hampshire]]. Incumbent Republican Gov. [[Chris Sununu]] did not seek election to a fifth term.{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2023 |title=Chris Sununu will not run for re-election for fifth term as New Hampshire governor |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/chris-sununu-new-hampshire-governor-not-running-for-election-2024/ |access-date=July 19, 2023 |website=CBS News |language=en-US}} Primary elections took place on September 10, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-08-06 |website=NCSL}} [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former U.S. Senator [[Kelly Ayotte]] won the Republican nomination with 63% of the vote over former state senate president [[Chuck Morse]], and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former Manchester mayor [[Joyce Craig]] won the Democratic nomination with 48% of the vote over state executive councilor [[Cinde Warmington]]. Ayotte won the general election, defeating Craig by a 9.34% margin. The election was the closest gubernatorial race for a U.S. state in the 2024 cycle. Along with neighboring [[2024 Vermont gubernatorial election|Vermont]], this race was one of two Republican-held governorships up for election in 2024 in a state [[Joe Biden]] won in the [[2020 United States presidential election in New Hampshire|2020 presidential election]]. {{toclimit|3}} ==Background== New Hampshire is a Democratic-leaning state in [[New England]] with a pattern of [[split-ticket voting]]. Incumbent Republican governor [[Chris Sununu]] was narrowly elected in [[2016 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2016]] and won re-election in [[2018 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2018]], [[2020 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2020]], and [[2022 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2022]] despite Republican presidential candidate [[Donald Trump]] losing the state in both [[2016 United States presidential election in New Hampshire|2016]] and [[2020 United States presidential election in New Hampshire|2020]]. Sununu opted not to seek re-election in 2024. This race was widely considered a tossup due to the incumbent retiring, the state's pattern of ticket splitting, and the concurrent [[2024 United States presidential election in New Hampshire|2024 presidential election]].{{Cite web |title=2024 Governor Race ratings |url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/ratings/governor-race-ratings |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=The Cook Political Report |language=en}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== *[[Kelly Ayotte]], former [[U.S. senator]] (2011–2017){{Cite web |date=2024-09-11 |title=Former Sen.
